concepts.learning_objective: Describe how teeth and tongue begin breaking down food in the mouth.
Explain how saliva breaks down starch into sugar and how the iodine test shows this.
Explain how wave-like contraction and relaxation of the food pipe walls push food to the stomach.
State the roles of the digestive juice, acid and mucus secreted in the stomach.
Describe the roles of bile, pancreatic juice and intestinal juice in the small intestine.
Explain how finger-like projections of the small intestine help absorb nutrients into blood.
Explain how the large intestine absorbs water and salts and forms stool.
Relate fibre, fermented foods and gut bacteria to a healthy digestive system.
Explain rumination in grass-eating animals such as cows and buffaloes.
Describe how the gizzard helps birds break down food without teeth.
Trace the path of air from the nostrils to the alveoli and state the role of each part.
Explain the movements of the ribs and diaphragm during inhalation and exhalation.
Interpret the lime water test showing that exhaled air has more carbon dioxide.
Describe the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide between the alveoli and blood.
Distinguish breathing as a physical process from respiration as a chemical process.
State the role of the heart, blood and blood vessels in transport.
Explain how gills help aquatic animals exchange gases with water.
Relate the breathing organs of frogs and earthworms to their habitats.
